title: How is heap memory divided (Young Generation with Eden/Survivor, Old Generation, Metaspace)?

s1_definition.oneliner: Heap = Young Gen (Eden + 2 Survivors) + Old Gen. New objects go to Eden. Survivors hold objects that survived GC. Old Gen holds long-lived objects.
s1_definition.profdef:
- Young Gen: Eden + Survivor 0 + Survivor 1
- Old Gen (Tenured): objects surviving many minor GCs
- New objects → Eden; surviving → Survivor; old enough → Old Gen
- Young Gen is small and collected often (Minor GC)
- Old Gen is larger and collected rarely (Full GC)

sections.s6_takeaway:
Heap = Young Gen (Eden + 2 Survivors) + Old Gen. New objects go to Eden. Survivors hold objects that survived GC. Old Gen holds long-lived objects.\n\n

Remember one sentence: How is heap memory divided (Young Generation with Eden/Survivor, Old Generation, Metaspace) is fundamental knowledge for Java interviews and production banking work.
